discovery: Light-pulse atom interferometry as a precision instrument for inertial sensing and tests of fundamental physics

nominees.name: Christian J. Bordé
nominees.affiliation: LNE-SYRTE, Observatoire de Paris / CNRS, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Bordé showed that atomic recoil in optical transitions forms matter-wave beam splitters, which made the Ramsey-Bordé interferometer possible. Kasevich then demonstrated light-pulse atom interferometry with laser-cooled atoms. He developed it into gravimeters, gradiometers and gyroscopes of unprecedented stability, and into 10-metre fountains that test the equivalence principle with quantum objects. Müller extended these methods with large-momentum-transfer interferometry. His photon-recoil measurements gave one of the most precise determinations of the fine-structure constant, which confronts the electron g-2 test of QED. He also measured gravitational phase shifts, including a gravitational Aharonov-Bohm effect, and searched for dark-energy fields. Together they turned the wave nature of atoms into a metrological tool that complements optical clocks. It probes gravity, relativity and fundamental constants with laboratory precision, and it now serves in geodesy, navigation and proposed gravitational-wave detectors.
